title: OpenFinGym Multi-Task Quant Agent Evaluation on H026/H174 Tasks
description: Evaluate George's existing confirmed strategies (H026 ETF rotation, H174 PEAD-NLP) against the OpenFinGym benchmark framework (arXiv:2606.26350, Zhang et al. 2026, University of Edinburgh / UCL / Alan Turing Institute / Oxford). OpenFinGym provides: (1) a unified gym environment covering forecasting, strategy construction, real-time trading, and fraud detection; (2) an automated task-construction pipeline converting quant finance publications into executable task packages; (3) a containerized runtime with host-side verifier service that prevents train-test leakage; (4) a paper trading engine with low-latency data-stream design; (5) SFT and RL post-training integration. H389 Phase 1: Install OpenFinGym (pip install openfingym or from GitHub); encode H026 monthly ETF rotation as an OpenFinGym forecasting task (predict which ETF will rank #1 next month); encode H174 PEAD as a trading task (event-driven entry/exit on 8-K signal); run existing confirmed models against the benchmark verifier to get standardized performance scores. Phase 2: Use OpenFinGym's RL post-training to fine-tune a small LLM (Mistral 7B or GPT-4o-mini) on H174 task definitions, testing whether LLM-guided entry improves over pure FinBERT. Gate: Phase 1 — both strategies score above equal-weight/random baseline in OpenFinGym's verifier; Phase 2 — H174 LLM-augmented WR > 81.8%. IS: existing splits. Script: backtesting/daily/run_h390_openfingym.py (stub).
rationale: OpenFinGym (arXiv:2606.26350, June 2026) addresses the fragmented evaluation problem in LLM quant agents — existing platforms test single tasks and overstate competence. Encoding our confirmed strategies into OpenFinGym serves two purposes: (1) validation — independent verification that H026 and H174 produce genuine alpha rather than lookahead artifact; (2) upgrade path — OpenFinGym's RL post-training integration provides a structured path to the LLM-enhanced PEAD strategy (H274 multi-agent PEAD, H375 finetuned LLM PEAD) without building the evaluation harness from scratch. The containerized leakage-resistant verifier is particularly valuable given our documented H256 look-ahead bias incident (unlagged 12m signal inflated GEM+Sector OOS Sharpe from 0.646 to 1.956).
